newsitem.title: USA: Federated Investors in pact with Lehman.
newsitem.headline: Federated Investors in pact with Lehman.

text.p: Federated Investors and Lehman Brothers said Monday they had reached a definitive agreement enabling Federated to manage six Lehman institutional money market funds and to offer its own comparable funds to replace three Lehman retail money funds.
Financial terms were not disclosed. The completion is subject to shareholder approvals.
A statement issued by the firms said the move will allow both to further focus on their respective core businesses.

Under the agreement, a statement from the firms said, Federated will manage about $4 billion in institutional assets from the following six funds: Lehman Brothers Government Obligations, Prime Value, Prime Money Market, Lehman Treasury Instruments II, Municipal Money Market and Tax-Free Money Market.

And Federated will offer its own retail money market funds - Automated Cash Management Trust Cash II Shares, Municipal Cash Series II, and New York Municipal Cash Trust Institutional Service Shares. These will replace Lehman Brothers Daily Income, Municipal Income and New York Municipal funds, which total about $1 billion in assets, the statement said.
Under the agreement, Lehman Brothers' 300 investment representatives will also use Federated funds for their cash sweep accounts, the statement said.
